provenance: Prepared and read immutable current packets; compared authored prose with selected declarations and tests during the 2026-10-24 lean-ification. The reviewer integrated the surrounding documentation and earlier evidence tooling changes; the mutual selector implementation was authored by a separate subagent. This is an agent review, not a human sign-off or a Lean proof.
rationale: Inventory::inputs starts from add_unit, whose implementation I read in tool:mdbook-dada/src/inventory.rs: it records the entire raw unit, exact selected Lean or Rust/test bodies, and recursively referenced units. It then adds configured policies/context, Cargo and book metadata, tooling sources/tests including Lean fixtures, and conservative full Lean context where applicable. validate_bundle independently reconstructs that expected set and compares identity, path, contents and hash after integrity checks; an exact selection cannot be replaced by its containing-file context. The missing/substituted-input test repackages internally consistent digests after removing required keys or altering a selected body, and still expects failure. The fixture-freshness test checks omission and mutation of a renderer Lean fixture. The body correctly excludes semantic correspondence from this syntactic check. I reviewed its explicit dependencies closed_body, configuration and exact_selection against their selected implementations/tests too, including the current mutual-selection extension.
limitations: Correspondence was assessed by inspection under the recorded policy; passing syntactic validation does not prove this reasoning correct.
Mechanical execution results are reported separately. Full context/tool snapshots were consulted at the relevant helpers; unrelated declarations and all proof tactics were not audited.
